newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: INFLATION LOW BUT INTEREST RATES "QUITE HIGH" - HOWARD
Prime Minister, John Howard, says he's proud that Australia Continues to boast very low levels of inflation.
Mr Howard told a mining industry dinner in Canberra interest rates have fallen rapidly, but are still relatively high by the standards of the industrialised world.
He says the Government's goal is to provide a stable, low inflation environment.
HOWARD COMES ON STRONG FOR TAX REFORM
Prime Minister, John Howard, has told a mining industry dinner in Canberra it is vital Australians have a serious and thorough debate on tax reform.
Mr Howard says anyone who understands the challenges to Australia's economy must acknowledge the tax system is less than perfect, calling it the nation's last outpost of economic backwardness.
He says reforming the system won't be easy, but it must be undertaken if this generation of political and industry leaders are to avoid letting down generations to come.
Mr Howard says a new taxation system needs to be established for the new millenium.
FIGURES TIPPED TO SHOW A SLOWLY IMPROVING ECONOMY

The release today of current account deficit numbers, figures for motor vehicle registrations, and last month's retail trade snapshot are expected to give an indication about how the economy is travelling.
The current account deficit for March is expected to show an improvement, with the median forecast for a A$4.8 billion deficit.
Motor vehicle registrations for April are tipped to fall, but there's expected to be good news for retailers, with a predicted rise in sales of point-seven of a per cent for April.
Chief Economist at Colonial State Bank, Hans Kunnen, says this rise is in part a result of lower interest rates, and shows the economy is in reasonable shape.
Mr Kunnen says the economy is improving, but not quickly enough to eat into unemployment.
16 YEAR OLD TO FACE MURDER CHARGE
A 16-year-old boy will appear in Maitland Children's Court, near Newcastle in New South Wales, this morning, charged with the murder of 47-year-old Metford man, Philip White.
Mr White's battered body was found by his family in a park behind Metford Public School yesterday morning.
Police believe he was attacked shortly after getting off a train at Metford Station on his way home on Wednesday night.
The boy was taken into custody late yesteRday and charged by Maitland detectives overnight.
He's been refused bail, and will appear in Court this morning.
Detectives have also charged a 17-year-old youth with concealing a serious offence.
AFP'S PROBLEMS IN THE PAST COULD BE LINKED TO TODAY
Australian Federal Police Commissioner, Mick Palmer, says bad procedural practices in the eighties, could be linked to some of today's problems within the force.
An independent inquiry into alleged corruption within the AFP by Sydney Lawyer Ian Harrison, has found no systemic corruption in the force.
However, eight officers accused of inappropriate behaviour have been asked to show cause why their employment shouldn't be terminated.
AFP Commissioner, Mick Palmer, says the report has highlighted some of the mistakes made in the past, but says most have now been addressed as part of the AFP's reforms.
SENATE BY-PASS AN ACT OF CONTEMPT: OPPOSITION
The Federal Opposition has described as an act of contempt, threatened action by the Government to by-pass the Senate over changes to the CES.
Employment Minister, Amanda Vanstone, says she'll do just that, if the Senate frustrates the thrust of the reforms.
The Opposition, Democrats and Greens are demanding changes to the plan which would open up the CES to competition from private companies.
Senator Vanstone says she doesn't mind appropriate amendments, but says she'll implement the plan under current legislation if necessary.
She says the first tender round for the services is worth A$2 billion and can't be held up because of parliament's indecision.
HANSON BEING CHARGED A FORTUNE FOR NEWCASTLE MEETING
One Nation party leader, Pauline Hanson, has been charged double the going rate by the Newcastle city council-owned Civic Theatre to use the venue for a speech tonight.
The meeting organiser says the price hike, to $16,500, almost makes the meeting unviable, but the council says the money will be used to pay for extra security to ward off demonstrators.
The council is worried that a planned peaceful demonstration may get out of hand.
But it is backing an alternative to tonight's One Nation meeting - a celebration of culture at the nearby Civic Park called the Cultural Stomp.
CRICKET: TAYLOR'S FORM NOT MUCH IMPROVED
In cricket, Australian skipper, Mark Taylor, has made just 30 in the second innings of the three day match against Gloucestershire.
Resuming at 19 not out, Taylor added just 11 before being dismissed LBW.
Taylor says he was disappointed, because he was starting to hit the ball in the middle, but failed to go on with the innings.
But there was bright news elsewhere in Australia's batting ranks, with opener Matthew Elliot making 124, and number three, Justin Langer, compiling 152 not out.
The game ended in a draw when Australia declared its second innings closed at four for 354.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
